report.summary:
The migration is still partway through. 8 of the 48 scripts pass reconcile. I re-ran reconcile myself on g01–g04, and all four match the legacy output exactly. For g07–g10 the converters reported a match from their own reconcile runs, but I have not re-run those four myself. None of the scripts has been code-reviewed. The other 40 scripts have not been started: g05, g06, g11–g31 and the dependent scripts g32–g48. One suspected legacy bug was found, in g09: an unshipped order is picked as the customer's first order in fulfilment order. The migrated job keeps that behaviour and it is recorded as a legacy bug. The general rules from the platform notes were applied to every comparison:
- String comparisons ignore case and trailing spaces.
- CAST to DECIMAL and ROUND use round-half-even.
- Integer division truncates toward zero.
- TOP n WITH TIES becomes RANK() <= n.
- NULLs sort first in ASC and last in DESC.
- ZEROIFNULL becomes COALESCE.

traps: the segment comparison ignores case and trailing spaces in session mode, so both sides are wrapped in lower(rtrim())
TRIM is written as trim(x, ' ') so it removes only spaces
status IN (...) ignores case and trailing spaces, so the column and the literals are both wrapped in lower(rtrim())
the channel comparison ignores case and trailing spaces, so it uses lower(rtrim())
explicit casts make the output types match the legacy table
the sku join (a CHAR(10) column) ignores case and trailing spaces, so both sides are wrapped in lower(rtrim())
ZEROIFNULL becomes COALESCE(x, 0) in both places it is used; the converter's reconcile reported a match, not yet re-run by me
integer division uses //, which truncates toward zero; the converter's reconcile reported a match, not yet re-run by me
NULLS FIRST is made explicit in the window ORDER BY to match Teradata's ASC ordering; the converter's reconcile reported a match, not yet re-run by me
suspected_legacy_bugs: An unshipped order (NULL ship_date) is picked as the first order in fulfilment order, for 117 of 266 customers on dataset A. Reproduced for parity.

traps: DATE - DATE gives a whole number of days on both platforms; explicit casts make the output types match; the converter's reconcile reported a match, not yet re-run by me

risks: 40 scripts have not been started. The dependent scripts g32–g48 cannot be reconciled until the scripts they depend on are saved.
g07–g10 have only the converters' own reconcile results; I have not re-run them.
None of the conversions has been code-reviewed.
g10 cross-joins etl_control. If that table ever holds more than one row, cust_id will no longer be unique. The legacy job behaves the same way.
Only 4 subagents can run at once, which slows the remaining work.
